titleEn: Book of the Dead of Ani — The weighing of the heart
about: The judgment scene that fills Plates 3 and 4 of the papyrus, after the hymn to Osiris on Plate 2: Ani's heart is weighed on a balance before the gods, and the words written around the picture tell the story. First comes Spell 30B, in which Ani begs his heart not to stand up as a witness against him; then the words of Anubis at the balance, Thoth's report that the heart has been judged and no wrong found, and the gods' verdict that Ani is true and that Ammit, the beast waiting to swallow a heart found wanting, shall have no power over him. Horus then brings Ani to Osiris, and Ani, kneeling before the god, asks to be counted among his favoured ones.

sentences.i: Said by the Osiris, the scribe Ani:
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ḏd in 'said by' in red, the usual heading of a speech. ḏd 'say' is the cobra ḏ and the hand d; the three strokes under them are not read (Budge's type shows nothing more, though they may stand for mdw 'words', as in the formula ḏd mdw 'words spoken'). in 'by' names the speaker: the reed i and a pot-shaped sign that writes in (coded W25), the reed repeating its i. Wsir 'Osiris' is written here with a long low seat (coded Q2, approximate) and the eye, without the seated god, a short writing used throughout the papyrus. Wsir N, 'the Osiris N', is the title of the dead: Ani is called by the god's name because he hopes to live again as Osiris did. sš 'scribe' is the scribe's palette with its water-pot and pen-case, a word-sign (Budge reads it ān). ꜣny 'Ani' is the vulture ꜣ, water n, three strokes (not read), two reeds i and a seated man as classifier. This is the heading of Spell 30B, the spell that keeps the heart from speaking against its owner when it is weighed; on the papyrus it is written above the picture of the weighing.

sentences.l: says-he · heart-my · of · mother-my · twice · heart-my · of · forms-my
sentences.i: He says: My heart of my mother! (Twice.) My heart of my forms of being!
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ḏd·f 'he says' in red: the verb ḏd and the horned viper f, the suffix pronoun 'he, his', which is joined to the word before it (written ·f). Ani speaks to his heart with two words for it. ib·i 'my heart' is the heart-sign ib with its stroke and the seated man, the suffix ·i 'I, my'. n is the genitive 'of'. mwt·i 'my mother' is the vulture mwt with t as complement, a seated woman as classifier and ·i; Budge restores the woman and the seated man in square brackets, where the papyrus is damaged. sp sn, the threshing floor sp and two strokes sn 'two', means 'twice': an instruction to say the words again, not part of the address. ḥꜣty·i 'my heart' is the forepart of a lion ḥꜣt with t as complement, two strokes y and the heart as classifier: the heart in the breast. ḫprw·i 'my forms, my modes of being' is the scarab ḫpr with r as complement, the chick w, a small mummy and a stroke as classifiers, and ·i (restored by Budge): ḫprw is the noun from ḫpr 'come into being', the shapes a being takes in its life. The heart was left in the body at mummification because it was to be weighed at the judgment.

sentences.i: Do not stand up against me as a witness.
sentences.n: m here is not the preposition: before a verb it is the negative imperative 'do not!' (from the verb imi 'not to do'), written with the owl m. ꜥḥꜥ 'stand, stand up' is the mast ꜥḥꜥ with the arm ꜥ as complement and walking legs as classifier of movement; after m it takes the form called the negatival complement. r·i 'against me' is the mouth r with ·i. m 'as' is the owl again, now the preposition. mtr 'witness' is the phallus mt with t as complement, the mouth r, one stroke and two strokes, and as classifier a seated man who seems to raise his hand to his mouth (the figure of speaking; it may be the plain seated man). The heart knew everything its owner had done and could testify against him before the gods.

sentences.i: Do not oppose me in the tribunal.
sentences.n: m 'do not!' is written here with the other common sign for m (Aa15). ḫsf 'oppose, repel' is one sign in Budge's type, a spindle with the horned viper at its foot (coded U35), which writes ḫsf by itself. r·i 'against me'; m 'in'. ḏꜣḏꜣt 'tribunal, council' is the fire-drill ḏꜣ written twice, with t. Between the two drills stand a small pot (coded W24, approximate) and a rod with three upright ticks (coded O29, approximate): Budge's type does not show what they are, and they are not read. A seated god and a stroke classify the word as a body of gods. The ḏꜣḏꜣt is the court of gods that sits at the judgment.

sentences.l: do-not · make · hostility-your · against-me · in-the-presence-of · the-keeper · of-the-balance
sentences.i: Do not show your hostility to me in the presence of the keeper of the balance.
sentences.n: m 'do not!' with irt, the eye ir and t: after m the verb takes the form called the negatival complement, here written with t. rq·k 'your hostility' is the mouth r, the hill-slope q and a wavy line ending in a loop (coded as the snake I14, approximate; it may be a cord) as classifier, then the basket k, the suffix ·k 'you, your'. rq is 'turn aside, oppose'; here it is a noun, the object of irt: 'do not make your hostility'. r·i 'against me'. m-bꜣḥ 'in the presence of' is m with the phallus-with-issue sign bꜣḥ 'presence', a stroke and the papyrus roll. iry mḫꜣt 'the keeper of the balance': iry 'one who belongs to' (reed i, mouth r, two strokes y), and mḫꜣt 'balance', written with a picture of the balance itself. The keeper of the balance is the god who works the scales; in the picture below it is Anubis.

sentences.l: you · ka-my · which-is-in · body-my · Khnum · who-makes-sound · limbs-my
sentences.i: You are my ka, which is in my body, the Khnum who keeps my limbs sound.
sentences.n: ntk 'you' is the independent pronoun (water n, loaf t, basket k): ntk N is 'you are N', a sentence with no verb. kꜣ·i 'my ka' is the two raised arms kꜣ with ·i. imy 'which is in' is the nisba of m 'in', written with one sign for im (Aa13); its ending y is not written. ẖt·i 'my body' is an animal's belly ẖ, t, a stroke and ·i. Next comes ḫnmw 'Khnum', the jug ḫnm with m as complement; no god classifier is written, and the group could be taken as a verb, but a name fits the sentence best: 'you are my ka …, (you are) Khnum'. swḏꜣ 'who makes sound, who keeps whole' is the causative of wḏꜣ 'be sound': bolt s, chick w, fire-drill ḏꜣ with the vulture ꜣ as complement; a participle. ꜥwt·i 'my limbs' is the arm ꜥ, t, a small sign of flesh (F51) and a stroke as classifiers, and ·i; the w of the plural is not written. The ka is the life-force a person is born with; Khnum, the ram-headed god, shapes the body on his potter's wheel.

sentences.l: go-forth · for-yourself · to · the-place · good · hasten(?)-I · there
sentences.i: Go forth to the good place to which I hasten(?).
sentences.n: pr 'go forth!' is the house pr with r as complement and walking legs: the imperative of pri. Budge prints it with n·k as one group, though his line number 11 stands between them; it is split here into pr and n·k 'for yourself' (water n and ·k), the dative that often follows a verb of motion in the imperative. It could also be read as one verb, pr·n·k 'you have gone forth', but a command suits the address. r 'to'. bw 'place' is the foot b alone, its w not written; nfr 'good' is the heart and windpipe. The next sign is uncertain: a tall bound bundle notched at the top, coded V33 as the nearest shape. Budge reads it ḥen with his own question mark, and ḥn 'hasten' is kept here only as his guess. The reed i after it, which Budge prints as a separate word, is joined to it as the suffix ·i 'I'. im 'there' (reed and m) points back to bw nfr: 'the good place that I hasten (to) there', that is, 'to which I hasten'. The good place is the next world of the blessed.

sentences.i: Do not make my name foul(?) to the entourage.
sentences.n: m 'do not!'. The verb is the bolt s, the placenta ḫ and the mouth r, then a band with hanging strands (coded Aa30, approximate) and a slim fish (coded K5, approximate) as classifiers: sḫr. A fish classifies words of stench, and Budge reads 'make to stink'; but s-ḫ-r is not a usual spelling of any such word: these signs ordinarily spell sḫr 'overthrow, fell' (the causative of ḫr 'fall'), which takes no fish. The sense is uncertain. rn·i 'my name' is r and n, a man with his hand to his mouth as classifier, and ·i. n 'to' is the preposition. šnyt 'the entourage, the court' (Budge: Shenit) is a loop of rope šn with n as complement, two reeds y, t, a standing man with a staff (approximate) and a stroke: the collective noun from šni 'surround', those who stand around a god. The name was part of the person; to make it stink was to harm him.

sentences.l: do-not · speak · lies · against-me · beside · the-god
sentences.i: Do not tell lies against me beside the god.
sentences.n: m 'do not!'; ḏd 'say, speak' (cobra and hand). grg 'lies, falsehood' is a single sign, a pick on a stand (U17), which writes grg. r·i 'against me'. r-gs 'beside, at the side of' is the mouth r, then the sign Aa15, which writes m, with a stroke. Read as printed, r and m, it gives Budge's erma 'near'; it is taken here as the similar sign Aa13, which writes gs 'side' and with which the papyrus writes r-gs in the rubric of Spell 125. The two signs are easily confused, but the reading is not sure. nṯr 'the god' is the cloth on a pole, the flag-like sign nṯr. The god is the judge before whom the heart is weighed.

sentences.i: How good! It is good that you hear …
sentences.n: nfr wy 'how good!': nfr (heart and windpipe) and the particle wy 'how …!' (chick w and two strokes), which Budge prints as one word with it; they are split here. nfr sḏm·k: nfr again, now the predicate, and sḏm·k, the ear sḏm with m as complement and ·k, a sḏm·f form standing as the subject: 'good (is it that) you hear'. Ani's address to his heart ends here in mid-phrase; Budge prints dots in his English. His footnote shows that the papyrus of Hunefer ends the spell earlier, after the word for the court, and that later papyri go on with a further petition and a closing wish.

sentences.l: said · by · He-who-is-in-the-embalming-place · give · face(?) · the-one · who-judges · truth-[…] · of · the-balance · to · its-standing
sentences.i: Said by He who is in the Place of Embalming: Pay heed(?), you who judge what is right […] of the balance, so that it stands upright.
sentences.n: Written above the head of Anubis, who kneels at the balance in the picture: a legend, not part of Ani's spell. ḏd in 'said by'. imy-wt 'He who is in the place of embalming', a title of Anubis, is the sign im (Aa13) and a small looped cord (coded V38, approximate) for wt 'embalming place', with t; Budge prints the two as separate words, joined here. imi 'give!' (reed i, m twice, and the arm), the imperative of rdi, with ḥr 'face' (face and stroke) may be 'give (your) face', that is, 'pay heed'; the 'your' is not written and the reading is not sure. pꜣ wḏꜥ mꜣꜥt 'the one who judges what is right': pꜣ 'the' is the duck pꜣ (coded G41; the print does not show clearly whether it is the flying duck G40, the usual sign for pꜣ); wḏꜥ 'judge' is the stand-like sign Aa21 alone, a participle after the article; mꜣꜥt 'truth' is the plinth mꜣꜥ, t and two strokes. After mꜣꜥt the papyrus is damaged: Budge shows a hatched gap about one and a half groups wide, with dots under it, and what stood there is lost. n mḫꜣt 'of the balance'. r ꜥḥꜥw·s: r 'to, so that' with ꜥḥꜥw, the mast, the arm and the chick w, and ·s 'its' (the bolt), referring to the balance (feminine): 'so that it stands (true)'. With the gap, the grammar of the whole is uncertain.

sentences.l: said · by · Thoth · who-judges-truth · of · the-Ennead · of-gods · great · who-are · in-the-presence-of · Osiris
sentences.i: Said by Thoth, who judges what is right for the great Ennead of the gods who are in the presence of Osiris:
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ḏd in in red, the head of Thoth's speech; ḏḥwty goes on in black. ḏḥwty 'Thoth' (Budge: Teḥuti) is the ibis on its standard with t and two strokes y as complements. The next group is one printed sign: the horns wp with the feather of mꜣꜥt rising from between them. It is read wp-mꜣꜥt 'who judges what is right', wp from wpi 'open, separate, judge' and mꜣꜥt its object; Budge reads àp maā, 'the righteous judge'. n 'of'. psḏt nṯrw ꜥꜣt 'the great Ennead of the gods': psḏt is the Ennead, the company of nine gods, written with a disc crossed by a line and t. The type's sign is coded X6, the round loaf (approximate), but the word needs the moon-sign psḏ (N9), a disc cut across by a line, which the printed shape resembles. Budge reads paut, his reading of this word; pꜣwt 'loaves, cake-offerings', the word the loaf X6 writes, does not fit a body of gods that sits in judgment and speaks. The god-sign nṯr is written three times for the plural nṯrw; ꜥꜣt 'great' (column ꜥꜣ and t) is feminine to agree with psḏt. nty 'who' (n, t, two strokes). m-bꜣḥ wsir 'in the presence of Osiris': here Osiris is the god himself, written with the seat, the eye and the seated god. Thoth, the scribe of the gods, records the result of the weighing.

sentences.i: Hear this speech.
sentences.n: sḏm·tn 'hear!' is the ear sḏm with m as complement and ·tn 'you' (plural): t, n and plural strokes, the suffix for several people. With a suffix the verb is a wish or command: 'may you hear, hear!'. ḏdt 'speech, words' is the noun from ḏd 'say': the hand d and the cobra ḏ (printed in the reverse of their usual order), t, and the man with hand to mouth as classifier of speech. pn 'this' (stool p and water n) is the masculine form, though ḏdt is feminine; the copy does not keep the agreement.

sentences.l: in · being · true · (iw) · have-judged-(I) · the-heart · of · the-Osiris
sentences.i: Truly, I have judged the heart of the Osiris.
sentences.n: m wn mꜣꜥ 'in truth, truly' is a fixed phrase: m 'in', wn 'being' (the hare wn with n as complement), mꜣꜥ 'true' (the sickle mꜣ and the plinth mꜣꜥ); literally 'in true being'. iw (reed and chick) opens the statement. wḏꜥ 'judge' is the stand-like sign Aa21. Budge prints the water n after it as a separate word, but it belongs to the verb: wḏꜥ·n is the sḏm·n·f, the form that marks a completed action ('has judged', 'judged'), the n written between the verb and its subject. The subject ·i 'I' is not written, as often in this papyrus; Thoth is speaking. Budge reads 'is weighed'; the n makes it Thoth's own report. ib 'heart' (heart and stroke); n 'of'; wsir 'the Osiris', here Ani, written with the eye, the throne and the seated god.

sentences.i: His ba stands as a witness concerning him.
sentences.n: iw opens a new statement. bꜣ·f 'his ba' is a bird with a human head (coded G53), a bowl of incense before it, and ·f. ꜥḥꜥ 'standing' is the mast ꜥḥꜥ, the arm ꜥ as complement and walking legs: the stative after its subject, 'his ba (is) standing'. m mtr 'as a witness', the same word as in Ani's plea, with the same doubtful seated figure as classifier. r·f 'concerning him' (mouth r and ·f). The ba is the part of a person that moves freely after death, drawn as a human-headed bird; Ani asked his heart not to bear witness against him, and here it is his ba that stands as witness.

sentences.i: His case is right upon the great balance.
sentences.n: sp·f 'his case, his deed' is the bolt s, the stool p and the threshing floor sp as classifier, with ·f: sp is 'occasion, deed, matter'. mꜣꜥ 'true, right' after its subject is the stative: 'his case is right'. (An adjective as predicate stands first, as mꜣꜥ mty does in the gods' speech.) ḥr 'upon' (face and stroke). mḫꜣt 'the balance'. wr 'great' is the swallow wr with r as complement; to agree with the feminine mḫꜣt it should be wrt, and the t is not written.

sentences.i: No wrong of his could be found at all.
sentences.n: n 'not' is the two arms held apart (D35), here without water n. gm·n·tw 'has been found' is the ibis gm with m as complement, the n of the sḏm·n·f, and the ending tw (t and the coil w) that makes the verb passive; Budge's line number 22 stands inside the word. n with the sḏm·n·f does not, in the classical language, state a past act (that is n with the sḏm·f, as in the lines that follow); it says what does not or cannot happen: 'no wrong of his could be found'. In copies of this time it may also stand for the past, 'has not been found'; the sense is much the same. bṯꜣ·f 'his wrongdoing' is the foot b and the loaf t, then a cup-shaped sign (coded W10, approximate) where the tethering rope ṯ is expected, the sparrow as classifier and ·f. The t and the ṯ are both written because the two sounds had fallen together by this time; the ꜣ is not written. The sparrow classifies what is small, bad or wrong. nb 'any' (the basket) follows its noun.

sentences.i: He has not diminished the food offerings in the temples.
sentences.n: n 'not' with ḫbꜣ·f 'he diminished': the placenta ḫ and the foot b, a sign like a plough or hoe (coded U13, approximate) as classifier, and ·f; the ꜣ is not written. n with the sḏm·f, in a statement about what someone has done, is 'he did not, he has not'. šbw 'food, food offerings' is the pool š, the foot b, the chick w, a hatched loaf (coded X4, approximate) and plural strokes. m 'in'. r-prw 'temples, chapels' is the mouth r with a stroke, a second stroke, the house pr, plural strokes, the town sign and plural strokes again: r-pr 'temple' in the plural. To reduce a temple's offerings is one of the wrongs denied in the Confession of Spell 125.

sentences.i: He has not damaged what was made.
sentences.n: n ḥḏ·f 'he did not damage': the mace ḥḏ with the cobra ḏ curled round it as complement (one printed sign), the crossed sticks (Z9) as classifier of breaking and harm, and ·f; Budge's line number 23 stands inside the word. iryt 'what has been made' is the eye ir, the mouth r as complement, two reeds y, t and plural strokes: the feminine passive participle of iri 'make, do', used as a noun, 'what was made, works'. Budge renders it 'in deed'; as the object of ḥḏ it is what Ani did not damage. The reading is possible but not certain.

sentences.l: not · went-he · with · mouth-his · evil-things(?) · since · was-he · upon · earth
sentences.i: He did not go about with evil(?) in his mouth while he was on earth.
sentences.n: n šm·f 'he did not go': a pool with walking legs (N40) writes šm 'go', with ·f. ḫr 'with' is a single sign, the butcher's block ḫr (T28). rꜣ·f 'his mouth': mouth, stroke and ·f. nkꜣw is n, the basket k, the vulture ꜣ, the chick w and plural strokes; the word is rare and its sense uncertain. Budge reads 'evil things', and the sentence points to evil talk, but the meaning is not sure. ḏr 'since, when' is the sign ḏr with r as complement; before a verb it is a conjunction. wnn·f 'he was' is the hare wn and two waters n, the doubled form wnn of the verb 'be', with ·f. tp tꜣ 'upon earth': the head tp with its stroke and the strip of land tꜣ. tp tꜣ is the world of the living, as against the world below.

sentences.l: said · by · the-Ennead · of-gods · great · to · Thoth · who-is-in · Hermopolis
sentences.i: Said by the great Ennead of the gods to Thoth, who is in Hermopolis:
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ḏd in psḏt in red, the head of the gods' answer; nṯrw ꜥꜣ goes on in black. psḏt nṯrw 'the Ennead of the gods', as in Thoth's title, with the same disc-sign (coded X6, approximate). ꜥꜣ 'great' is the arm ꜥ as complement before the column ꜥꜣ, and under them a low bar with a small cup on it (coded R4, approximate) that is not read; the feminine t is not written. n 'to' is the preposition: the gods answer Thoth. imy ḫmnw 'who is in Hermopolis': imy (Aa13, its y unwritten) and ḫmnw (Budge: Khemennu), written with eight strokes, the number eight, ḫmnw, for the eight first gods of the town. Hermopolis in Middle Egypt was Thoth's city.

sentences.l: ordains(?)-he · (n) · it · this · which-comes-forth · from · mouth-your
sentences.i: What comes forth from your mouth is ordained(?).
sentences.n: The papyrus writes the first three words in red. The first sign is not clear in Budge's type: a pole with a hook at the top and a loop at the foot, coded V25 (wḏ 'command, ordain') as the nearest sign. Budge prints dots under it and does not read it, though his English has 'Decreed'. With the horned viper it is read wḏ·f 'he ordains', followed by n (water) and st 'it' (bolt and loaf, the dependent pronoun); but how the three words go together is not clear, and the whole is uncertain: the translation gives only the general sense. nn 'this' is the rush written twice with two water signs, the demonstrative standing before what it points to. prrt 'what comes forth' is the house pr, r twice, t and walking legs: the participle of pri with its r doubled, the form for what happens again and again, feminine for 'that which'. m rꜣ·k 'from your mouth' (mouth, stroke and ·k): Thoth's words.

sentences.l: true · exact · the-Osiris · scribe · Ani · true-of-voice
sentences.i: True and exact is the Osiris, the scribe Ani, true of voice.
sentences.n: mꜣꜥ mty 'true and exact': mꜣꜥ (sickle and plinth) and mty, the phallus mt with t as complement, two strokes y and the papyrus roll as classifier of an idea: 'exact, precise, upright'. The two adjectives come first as the predicate, with no verb: 'true and exact (is) the Osiris Ani'. Wsir sš ꜣny 'the Osiris, the scribe Ani', as in the heading. mꜣꜥ-ḫrw 'true of voice, vindicated' is written short, the plinth mꜣꜥ and the oar ḫrw: the epithet of the dead whose words were found true at the judgment. Here the gods give it to Ani.

sentences.i: He has not sinned, he has done no harm(?) to us.
sentences.n: n 'not' (arms and water n). bṯꜣ·f 'he sinned' is the same word as in Thoth's report, now a verb: foot b, loaf t, the cup-like sign for ṯ (approximate), the crossed sticks and the sparrow as classifiers, and ·f. n sḫr·f: the same uncertain verb s-ḫ-r with the fringed sign (Aa30, approximate) as in Ani's address, here without the fish; 'he did not do harm(?)'. ḫr·n 'towards us, against us' is the placenta ḫ and the mouth r, the preposition ḫr used of persons, and ·n 'we, us' (water n with plural strokes). The gods speak of themselves.

sentences.i: Ammit shall not be allowed to prevail over him.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes the mouth r, t and the plain forearm ꜥ; read rdit, with the arm holding a loaf (di), the two arms being easily confused in the cursive hand. n rdit 'no letting': n 'not' with rdit, the infinitive of rdi 'give, let'; n before an infinitive denies it as a noun, 'there is no letting'. (The t could also begin the passive ending, n rdi·t(w) 'it is not allowed'; the sense is the same.) sḫm 'prevail, have power' is the sceptre sḫm with m as complement and a low sign (coded U15) as classifier; sḫm m is 'have power over'. ꜥm-mwt 'Ammit' (Budge: Amemet), 'Swallower of the dead': the arm ꜥ and the owl m for ꜥm 'swallow', then the owl m and t for mwt 'the dead' (its w not written), and as classifier a crouching beast with a long snout (coded E17, approximate). Budge's line number 29 stands before the classifier. im·f 'over him' is m in its form before a suffix, im, with ·f. In the picture Ammit, part crocodile, part lion, part hippopotamus, waits beside the balance to swallow a heart found wanting.

sentences.l: cause · be-given · to-him · offering-loaves · a-going-forth · in-the-presence-of · Osiris · a-field(?) · lasting · in · the-Field-of-Offerings · like · the-followers · of-Horus
sentences.i: Have offering loaves given to him, and a going forth into the presence of Osiris, and a lasting field(?) in the Field of Offerings, like the followers of Horus.
sentences.n: imi 'cause!' (reed, two m's, the arm), the imperative of rdi, with di·tw 'that there be given': the arm with loaf di, t and w, the passive of rdi. Budge prints di·tw n·f as one group; split here, n·f 'to him' (water n and ·f). snw 'offering loaves' is the bolt s, n as complement, the pot nw and w, a hatched loaf (approximate) and plural strokes. prt 'a going forth' is the infinitive of pri. m-bꜣḥ wsir 'into the presence of Osiris'. The next word begins with two uprights on a base (coded O22, approximate); Budge reads seḥ 'field'. It is taken, as in the hymn to Osiris, as ꜣḥt 'field', with t, a wedge of land (approximate) and a stroke; the first sign may be the pool with lotus flowers that writes ꜣḥ, but the reading is doubtful. mn 'lasting' (gaming board, n, papyrus roll) is the stative. sḫt-ḥtpw 'the Field of Offerings' (Budge: Sekhet-hetepu): the reeds sḫt with t, the land wedge and a stroke, then the offering mat ḥtp with a hatched loaf and a stroke. mi 'like' (milk jug and reed); šmsw 'followers' (the bundle šms, walking legs, plural strokes); ḥr 'Horus', the falcon. The Field of Offerings is the land of plenty of the blessed dead; the followers of Horus are the blessed of old.

sentences.i: Said by Horus, son of Isis:
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ḏd in ḥr 'said by Horus' in red. ḥr 'Horus' (Budge: Ḥeru) is the falcon with a stroke. sꜣ 'son' is the pintail duck sꜣ with its stroke. ꜣst 'Isis' (Budge: Àuset) is the seat ꜣs with t and the egg as classifier of a goddess. Horus, son of Osiris and Isis, leads Ani, now found true, to his father.

sentences.l: have-come-(I) · to-you · Wennefer · have-brought-(I) · to-you · the-Osiris · Ani
sentences.i: I have come to you, Wennefer, and I have brought you the Osiris Ani.
sentences.n: ii·n·i 'I have come' is the walking-legs sign ii (M18) with the reed and two strokes as complements, the walking legs as classifier, and n of the sḏm·n·f; the suffix ·i 'I' is not written. ḫr·k 'to you' is the preposition ḫr, used of going to a person (placenta ḫ and mouth r), with ·k. wnn-nfr 'Wennefer' (Budge: Un-nefer), 'he who is (always) perfect', a name of Osiris: the hare wn, two waters n, the heart and windpipe nfr and the seated god. in·n·i 'I have brought' is the pot in (W25) and n of the sḏm·n·f, its ·i again unwritten: ini 'bring'. Budge prints it as àn-nà-, running on into the next group. n·k 'to you' (water n and basket k). Wsir ꜣny 'the Osiris Ani', the seat written long and low (approximate) as before.

sentences.i: His heart is true, having come forth from the balance.
sentences.n: ib·f 'his heart' (heart, stroke, viper). mꜣꜥ 'true, right' is here the sickle mꜣ and the forearm ꜥ; after its subject it is the stative: 'his heart is true'. prt 'coming forth' is the house pr, r, t and walking legs, the infinitive of pri: the heart has come out of the weighing. m 'from'; mḫꜣt 'the balance'.

sentences.l: not · sinned-he · against · god · any · goddess · any
sentences.i: He has not sinned against any god or any goddess.
sentences.n: n bṯꜣ·f 'he has not sinned', written as in the gods' speech, here with the arms alone for n and the ṯ again the cup-like sign (approximate). ḫr 'against' is the preposition used of persons. nṯr nb 'any god': the god-sign nṯr with a seated god as classifier, and nb 'any' after it. nṯrt 'goddess' is the god-sign, t, the mouth r and a cobra as classifier of a goddess; the r, written after the t, repeats the last sound of nṯr. nb should be nbt to agree with nṯrt; the t is not written.

sentences.l: has-judged · it · Thoth · according-to · the-writing(?) · which-spoke · the-Ennead · of-gods · concerning-him
sentences.i: Thoth has judged it according to the writing(?) that the Ennead of the gods spoke concerning him.
sentences.n: wḏꜥ·n 'has judged': the chick w and the cobra ḏ as complements, then a small flat sign read as the hand d, which has no place in wḏꜥ and is not read (the cobra and hand are printed as the familiar pair of ḏd 'say'); it is coded as an unread sign, like the unread signs in ḏꜣḏꜣt, the stand-like sign wḏꜥ, and the n of the sḏm·n·f, which Budge prints as a separate word; joined here. sw 'it' (the sedge sw with the chick w as complement) is the dependent pronoun, the object: a pronoun object stands before a noun subject, here ḏḥwty 'Thoth'. m 'according to'. Then the scribe's palette (Y3) with a stroke: Budge reads àn 'decree'; taken here as sš 'writing, record', with doubt. ḏd·n 'which … spoke' is ḏd with the water n that Budge prints as the next word, joined here: the relative form of the sḏm·n·f, 'which the Ennead of the gods spoke'. psḏt nṯrw 'the Ennead of the gods' (the disc-sign again coded X6), nṯrw written with one god-sign and a stroke. r·f 'concerning him'.

sentences.i: It is exact, a great truth.
sentences.n: mty 'exact, upright', as in the gods' speech, here with the phallus-with-issue sign (D53) for mt, t, two strokes and the papyrus roll. mꜣꜥt 'truth, what is right' is the sickle mꜣ, the arm ꜥ and t. wr 'great' (swallow and r) follows its noun: mꜣꜥt wr(t) 'a great truth', the t of the feminine again unwritten. There is no verb: '(it is) exact, a great truth'.

sentences.l: cause · be-given · to-him · bread · beer · a-going-forth · in-the-presence-of · Osiris
sentences.i: Have bread and beer given to him, and a going forth into the presence of Osiris,
sentences.n: imi di·tw n·f 'let there be given to him', as in the gods' speech; Budge again prints di·tw and n·f as one group, split here. t 'bread' is the loaf t with a jug-like sign (coded W22, approximate), a hatched loaf (approximate) and plural strokes. ḥnqt 'beer' is the twisted wick ḥ and the hill-slope q with the beer jar and a stroke; its n and t are not written. pri 'a going forth' is the house pr with r and walking legs, the infinitive, its t unwritten. m-bꜣḥ wsir 'into the presence of Osiris'. Bread and beer were the staple food of Egypt and come first in every list of offerings.

sentences.i: and may he be like the followers of Horus for ever.
sentences.n: wnn·f 'he will be, may he be' is the hare wn with two waters n, the doubled form wnn of the verb 'be', and ·f; it looks forward. mi 'like' (the milk jug alone). šmsw ḥr 'the followers of Horus', as in the gods' speech, here with a stroke after the bundle. ḏt 'for ever' is the cobra ḏ, t and the strip of land: ḏt 'everlastingness', used as an adverb.

sentences.i: Said by the Osiris Ani:
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ḏd in in red. Budge prints no transliteration and no English under the cobra and hand; red, at the head of a speech and before in Wsir ꜣny, they can only be ḏd 'said'. in 'by' is the reed and water n (Budge's 'Behold' takes it differently). Wsir ꜣny 'the Osiris Ani'; Budge restores the water n and the three strokes of ꜣny in square brackets. The classifier is a man with one arm raised: Ani, kneeling before Osiris in the picture, now speaks for himself.

sentences.i: He says: See, I am in your presence, lord of the West.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ḏd·f 'he says' in red. mk 'see, behold' is the sign m (Aa15), the forearm and the basket k: the arm belongs to a later spelling of the word and is not pronounced. The pronoun 'I' that should follow is not written: 'see, (I am) in your presence'. m-bꜣḥ·k 'in your presence' is the compound preposition with ·k. nb imntt 'lord of the West': the basket nb with a seated god as classifier, and imntt 'the West', the emblem of the West with t written twice and a hill-like sign (coded N25, approximate) as classifier. The West, where the sun sets, is the land of the dead; its lord is Osiris.

sentences.i: There is no wrong in my body.
sentences.n: n 'there is no' (arms and water n) before a noun: a sentence that denies that something exists. isft 'wrong' is the reed i, a second narrow upright (its shape is not clear in Budge's type; taken as another reed), the bolt s, the viper f and the sparrow as classifier of bad things; the t is not written. m ẖt·i 'in my body': the belly sign ẖ, printed oddly (approximate), t, a stroke and ·i. isft is the opposite of mꜣꜥt.

sentences.i: I do not knowingly speak lies.
sentences.n: n ḏd·n·i 'I have not said': n with ḏd·n·i, the sḏm·n·f with ·i written this time (the seated man); n with the sḏm·n·f does not, in the classical language, state a past act (that is n with the sḏm·f, as in Thoth's report); it says what one does not or cannot do: 'I do not speak lies'. In copies of this time it may also mean 'I have not spoken'. grg 'lies' is the basket g and the mouth r as complements before the pick on its stand, grg. m rḫ 'knowingly', literally 'with knowledge': m and rḫ, the mouth r, the placenta ḫ and the papyrus roll.

sentences.i: There has been no second time(?).
sentences.n: n 'not' with sp 'occasion, time' (bolt s, stool p, threshing floor sp) and snnw 'second', the ordinal of sn 'two': two strokes for the number and the pot nw, the ending of the ordinal numbers. Literally 'not a second time'. It may mean that no fault was repeated, or that there was no double dealing (Budge: 'not have I acted with a double intent'); the sense is uncertain.

sentences.l: cause · be-I · like · the-favoured-ones · who-are · in-the-following-your
sentences.i: Let me be like the favoured ones who are in your following,
sentences.n: imi 'cause!' with wn·i 'that I be', the hare wn with n as complement and ·i: the sḏm·f after imi, 'let me be'. mi 'like' (jug and reed). ḥsyw 'the favoured ones' is the vase ḥs (W14) with two reeds y and a stroke: the passive participle of ḥsi 'praise, favour' used as a noun, its plural w not written. nty 'who'. m-ḫt·k 'in your following': a sign of two crossed planks (Z11) for m, the branch ḫt (approximate), t and a stroke, and ·k; m-ḫt is 'after, behind'.

sentences.l: the-Osiris · favoured · greatly · of · the-god · perfect · loved · of · the-lord · of-the-Two-Lands · royal · scribe · true · beloved-his · Ani · true-of-voice · before · Osiris
sentences.i: the Osiris, greatly favoured by the perfect god, loved by the lord of the Two Lands, the true royal scribe whom he loves, Ani, true of voice before Osiris.
sentences.n: The plea ends with Ani's titles. Wsir ḥsy ꜥꜣ 'the Osiris, greatly favoured' (Wsir N with Ani's titles between): ḥsy as just above, and ꜥꜣ 'greatly' (column, arm and papyrus roll) as an adverb. n nṯr nfr 'of the perfect god': nṯr nfr is the reigning king. mrr n nb tꜣwy 'loved of the lord of the Two Lands': mrr is the hoe mr with r twice, the participle 'loved' with its r doubled; nb tꜣwy 'lord of the Two Lands' (the land-strip written twice for the dual, each with a wedge of land, approximate) is the king again. sš nswt 'royal scribe' is written with nswt 'king' (the sedge) first, out of respect, though spoken after sš. mꜣꜥ 'true' (the plinth alone). mry·f 'his beloved' is the canal mr, two reeds y, a stroke and ·f: the passive participle 'loved by him', the king. ꜣny mꜣꜥ-ḫrw 'Ani, true of voice', here spelled with the sickle, the arm, the oar, the chick and the man with hand to mouth. ḫr wsir 'before Osiris': ḫr used of persons.
